title: scrim-onboard-quant-weekly-capture-apr21-2026
content:
Goal: capture the week’s runbook, quick experiment outcomes, and TODOs for the compact model onboarding pilot (KV-prefetch + 4-bit pathway).

Context / framing
- Team focus this sprint: reduce memory footprint for the 7B family while preserving scoring across our eval suites (safety-smoke, long-context coherence, streaming token stability).
- Onboarding candidate: ‘sparrow-7b-compact-v2’ (FP16 base converted with mixed 4-bit weight packing + per-channel scale table). Running initially on 80GB A100 dedicated nodes for latency profiling.
- Primary metrics we watch: token-level median latency (ms), tail-95 latency, token cost estimate (USD/token), eval passrate delta vs FP16 baseline (%), and KV cache integrity (misses per 10k requests).

Standup highlights (2026-04-21)
- Claire: finished baseline compare run (FP16 vs compact-v2) for the streaming-chat eval set (N=2.2k prompts). Preliminary: compact-v2 median latency down 18%, tail-95 down 25%, but hallucination rate (as measured by our retrieval-augmented truth-check) increased by 2.4 percentage points on short factuals.
- Arjun: rolled forward improved dequant kernel that fixes a sign-extension bug for attention keys. Re-ran microbenchmarks; KV regen reduced from 7% to 1.8% on cold-start tests. Patch in github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime#PR472.
- Maya: ran quality sweep on the safety-smoke eval set (200 prompts). Found 6 prompts with confidence drop below threshold; two of those are prompt-formatting edgecases (trailing markdown tables). Opened JIRA MLON-4321 to track.
- Ethan: end-to-end cost sim updated with new batching heuristics — recommends lowering max-batch-size from 64 to 48 for short requests to keep p95 under 180ms on Dedicated.

Experiment notes (quick captures)
1) Prefix caching + 4-bit combination
- Setup: enable prefix-KV caching on compact-v2 with conservative TTL=30s. Run: 5k short-chat interactions, 30% repeated prefixes.
- Outcome: effective token cost reduced by ~12% vs no-cache; median latency unchanged, p95 improved 9%. Observed cache invalidation bug when model variant rollouts happen (cache keys include model-version string; rollout generator emitted variant alias sometimes). Action: normalize rollout alias -> variant id in cache key (Arjun).

2) Dequant attention stability test
- Test: feed 512-token long-context prompts with adversarial token patterns (repeating numeric sequences) to catch KV drift.
- Outcome: 4-bit path had one reproducible divergence at step ~421 affecting later answer length heuristics. Root cause: kernel rounding-order when streaming flushes fractional accumulators. Mitigation: align rounding after fused matmul (patch queued). Risk: small throughput penalty (~1.6% compute). Decision: deploy mitigation to staging and re-run long-context eval set.

3) Eval regression sampler (small)
- Ran a targeted eval subset (250 prompts representing product-critical flows). compact-v2 dropped QA exact-match by 1.1%. Failures mostly short-span factuals; many recovered when we increased quant-rounding scale precision for token-embeds. Note: this tweak increases model size by ~0.7% memory.

Operational notes
- Canary rollout plan: canary traffic at 5% for 48 hours, monitor the following dashboards: per-prompt perplexity drift, rerank score delta, user-visible latency, errors/second. If any metric crosses threshold (perplexity +3 sigma or errors > 0.5/s per shard), auto rollback.
- Observability gaps: current tracing does not tag requests with quant-path metadata (qscheme:4bit, qscheme:4bit+pcscale). Add trace attribute and update Console dashboards (ticket: CONSOLE-1156).

Open questions / unresolved
- How to trade memory increase from selective higher-precision embeddings vs quality delta? We need a small user-impact study: pick 5 high-TSH product flows and simulate user-visible regressions if we keep embeddings in higher precision.
- Should rollout aliasing be reconciled in router layer or cache key generation layer? Short-term patch in runtime avoids alias issue; long-term solution likely in router to emit canonical ids.
- Are our eval sets representative enough for streaming use-cases? There are gaps in multi-turn streaming transcripts with heavy code-block formatting. Need to add 300 prompts sampled from recent production streaming traces (PII scrubbed) for a streaming-specific eval partition.

Action items (owner, ETA)
- Arjun: land dequant kernel patch and run full KV-regeneration suite (JIRA MLON-4317) — ETA 2026-04-25
- Maya: build additional streaming eval partition (300 prompts) and run safety + qa suites on compact-v2 — ETA 2026-04-28
- Ethan: update batching config in sim runner and re-run cost sim with TTL-based cache impact — ETA 2026-04-24
- Claire: draft canary rollout checklist + rollback thresholds for the compact-v2 pilot; coordinate with SRE for slowdown alarms — ETA 2026-04-23

Notes to self (scribbles)
- Remember: prefix keys should be (customer-id, model-id, model-version, prefix-hash) — avoid using ephemeral alias. Put this in onboarding checklist.
- Double-check that KPS (key prefetch service) honors model-version pinning; saw one event where a refresh used latest-latest causing mismatch.
- Keep a log of 1st-order hallucination examples from the 2.4% increase — we need a minimal prompt set to reproduce with deterministic seeds.

Meeting summary (weekly sync 2026-04-22)
- Quick recap of experiments above. Consensus: move forward with canary once dequant rounding patch is validated in staging.
- Decision to accept small memory increase for targeted embedding precision fixes if user-visible QA improves >1.5% on product-critical flows.
- Action: product-owner to sign off on canary thresholds by 2026-04-23.

Quick links & refs
- Kernel patch PR: github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/472
- Onboarding playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/compact-model-onboard+playbook
- Ticket tracking: JIRA-MLON-4321 (eval failures), MLON-4317 (kv-regeneration tests), CONSOLE-1156 (trace tags)

Next-week focus
- Validate rounding mitigation in staging, run full long-context eval set
- Finish streaming eval partition and re-run safety + QA
- Finalize canary checklist and coordinate with SRE for 5% traffic roll

End notes: keep this doc as ephemeral weekly capture; once canary completes and we have stable numbers move a sanitized summary to the onboarding playbook and create a permanent rollout runbook.
